specification.problem: Physical mapping of fault-tolerant quantum circuits (scheduling, placement, routing) onto Universal Logic Blocks, plus selecting a single best ULB size by weighting operation latencies with critical-path occurrence frequencies. The abstract gives no formal equations.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful construction: a weighted-latency ULB size selection criterion and a schedule latency with routing delays on a dependency DAG, with a generic force-directed scheduling force term as background. The full mapper (loose scheduling with no-cloning DFG transformation, timing-driven placement, dynamic routing) and the 40% experimental result are outside scope. No quantum circuit or state preparation is specified.

symbols.meaning: latency of FT operation o mapped onto ULB of size s
occurrence frequency of operation o on critical paths of the target algorithm
weighted latency for ULB size s
quantum data flow graph, a DAG whose edges are qubit dependencies
start time (schedule level) of operation v
routing latency between predecessor u and operation v, depending on placement

equations.label: Weighted ULB latency
equations.description: Weighted average latency of FT operations for ULB size s, weighted by critical-path frequency.
equations.abstract_quote: using information about the occurrence frequency of operations on critical paths of the target quantum algorithm to weigh these latencies
equations.justification: The abstract says latencies are weighed by critical-path occurrence frequency; a linear weighted sum is the simplest reading, but the exact weighting is not stated.

equations.label: Best ULB size
equations.description: Select the single ULB size minimizing weighted latency.
equations.abstract_quote: an approach is presented to determine the single best ULB size for a target quantum circuit
equations.justification: Choosing the best size by examining weighted latencies implies minimization; the details are not given.
assumptions: Minimization of weighted latency is the criterion

equations.label: Precedence with routing latency
equations.description: Start of an operation must follow its predecessor's completion plus the routing latency determined by placement distance.
equations.abstract_quote: resulting distances between predecessor and current operations, which in turn determines routing latencies
equations.justification: The abstract says placement distances determine routing latencies that influence scheduling; the additive form is a modeling assumption.
assumptions: Routing latency is additive between dependent operations

equations.label: Circuit latency
equations.description: Makespan to be minimized by the scheduler subject to eq_3 and resource constraints.
equations.justification: Standard makespan definition for DAG scheduling.

equations.label: Generic force-directed scheduling force
equations.description: Self-force of tentatively assigning operation v to level j, where DG is the distribution graph of resource usage per level and \Delta p_v is the change in v's probability at level k.
equations.justification: Classical force-directed scheduling background; the paper's modified version is not specified.
assumptions: Classical unmodified form; the paper's modification is unknown

steps.description: Build the quantum data flow graph and transform it to make the no-cloning constraint explicit (details not given).
Run loose force-directed scheduling to reduce resource contention and latency.
Place operations by timing-driven placement, iteratively calling the scheduler to correct levels.
Route qubits to obtain dynamic routing latencies r_uv.
For each candidate ULB size, compute weighted latency and select the best size.

specification.classical_postprocessing: Classical compilation flow only; no quantum measurement. Output is a schedule, placement, routing and chosen ULB size.
assumptions: Scope choice: a classical mapping and optimization problem with no quantum state evolution
Linear frequency-weighted latency and additive routing delay are assumed models
missing_information: Actual ULB definition and architecture model
